name: ECOS (India) Mobility & Hospitality Ltd
title: ECOS (India) Mobility & Hospitality Ltd - 544239 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% (from 12.0% a year ago) on ETS price competition; FY27 margin guidance cut to around 10% from 11–13%, while revenue guidance held at 15–18%.

summary.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 16.7% YoY to INR2,113.72 million and trips rose 27% YoY to about 1.48 million, with 61 new clients added. EBITDA was flat YoY at INR218.47 million, and margin fell to 10.3% from 12.0% a year ago and 11.7% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the drop to higher operating costs, a higher ETS mix and more intense pricing pressure, especially in ETS. The FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to around 10% from the earlier 11-13% range, while revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was retained.

segments.name: ETS (employee transportation services)
segments.commentary: 59% of revenue (up from 40% share implied by mix of prior year's 60:40 comparison noted on call; management said mix moved slightly toward CCR YoY). Pricing pressure is most intense here; management said margin erosion is more evident in ETS. 15 new ETS clients added in the quarter, described as one of the highest ever for ETS.

segments.name: CCR (chauffeur-driven car rentals)
segments.commentary: 41% of revenue. Management cited healthy recovery in corporate and travel mobility demand, though inbound international travel remains subdued. 46 new clients added, the majority by number.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin now expected around 10%, versus the earlier 11-13% range; management hopes to maintain margins at this level through the year.
Revenue growth guidance of 15% to 18% for FY27 was reiterated.
Employee cost expected to grow around 20% in FY27.
Operating leverage expected to kick in at a scale of over INR 1,000 crore of revenue; no timeline given.
B2C app launch expected this quarter; management set no high target for FY27 and promised guidance from next year.
Management is evaluating acquisitions after hiring a senior strategic finance professional last month; no buyback or shareholder return decision announced.
capex_capacity: Domestic footprint expanded to 151 cities, adding 20 in the quarter, from 130+ at end FY26.
Owned and vendor-operated fleet of about 19,500 vehicles as of June 30, 2026; the vast majority is vendor-supplied, keeping the model asset-light.
Management said 10,000-11,000 vehicles are used daily, with the rest held for demand spikes.
EV fleet increased to 460 vehicles from 390 at end Q4 FY26; EV adoption remains measured.
New CCR technology rolled out this quarter to automate contact centre, dispatch and billing; transition expected to settle within the quarter, with productivity gains to follow.
Upgraded proprietary technology platform completed this quarter; direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26.
demand_pricing: Trips of about 1.48 million in the quarter, up 27% YoY and ~7% QoQ; revenue grew slower than trips because of price reductions.
Active enterprise client base of about 1,400, up ~18% YoY; 61 new clients added vs 53 in Q1 FY26.
About 51% of revenue comes from customers with more than five years' relationship with ECOS.
Pricing pressure more intense than anticipated, particularly in ETS; management has set internal thresholds below which it will not bid, but did not disclose the level.
Gross margins declined as lower client rates were absorbed partly from vendor margins; management said it would negotiate harder with vendors.
Online/app bookings were about 14% of bookings in Q1, similar to 15-16% in Q4 FY26.
Management said few clients were lost to competition this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What changed since the 11-13% margin guidance, what is driving pricing pressure, and at what margin will the company walk away from business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition and pricing pressure were higher than anticipated, especially in ETS. It has set internal client-level thresholds below which it will not bid, and did not disclose a level; company-wide margin is expected to be held at around 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost savings and productivity be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Automation of CCR contact centre, dispatch, billing and booking, expected mainly to reduce employee expense and improve vehicle utilisation; management said it would also negotiate harder with vendors. Savings were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge given low entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three elements: long-standing enterprise relationships, a large reliable vendor supply base built over decades, and processes and people. It said the market is only 15-20% organised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins decline and how low can they go?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower rates given to win business are absorbed partly from vendor margins, most evident in ETS. Management declined to specify a floor but said it has internal thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: When and by how much will margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeline given; management said it is guiding to maintain margins because competition duration is uncertain, with operating leverage expected at a much larger scale (over INR 1,000 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Will ETS and CCR EBITDA margins be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said costs are shared across the organisation, so a segment EBITDA split is not practical to provide.

risks_watch: Margin trajectory: FY27 guided to ~10% after Q1 at 10.3%; 11-13% range has been withdrawn, and further cuts are possible if pricing pressure persists.
Employee cost growth of ~21.9% YoY vs revenue growth of 16.7% is compressing operating leverage; watch whether productivity from automation offsets it.
Gross margin erosion in ETS from new competitors entering the market.
Credit risk and client quality: management stresses high-quality enterprise wins, but pricing reductions may affect contract economics.
Capital allocation: INR1,558 mn cash with no clear acquisition or shareholder return plan; watch for M&A announcements.
Guidance credibility: an investor criticised the sudden guidance change within one quarter, and management said competitive behaviour is hard to predict.
Other expenses fell only because a prior-year one-time provision did not recur, so the base is not a structural saving.
key_quotes: And that is what the market dynamics are and that is what the ground reality is today especially in ETS.
However, the decline in the margins or the competitive pressure was higher than what we anticipated.
Yes, that's the million-dollar question. And at the same time, internally we have certain set, certain thresholds below which we would not go.
So, our guidance is that we would be maintaining this and because we are not sure of the longevity of this intensity of competition, how long is it going to last.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, volumes, footprint and balance sheet, but defensive and cautious on margins: management admitted pricing pressure was higher than anticipated and declined to name a margin floor, moderation outlook, or segment EBITDA. Guidance was framed as maintaining margins around 10% because competition duration is uncertain.

adds.what: Domestic footprint expanded to 151 cities (20 added in quarter; no new capacity capex stated)
B2C app launch (demand channel, not capacity)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was held (midpoint 16.5%), backed by trips up 27% YoY and 61 new clients, but no capacity capex is disclosed (asset-light vendor fleet), and EBITDA margin guidance was cut to around 10% amid pricing pressure.
